entrypoints.summary: An authenticated administrator changes post slugs through wp-admin Quick Edit and changes stylesheet and upload_path through options.php.
A front-end post request using the controlled post ID causes single-post template selection; request parameters are used in the PEAR and shell stages.

negative_controls: A hardened resolver should reject decoded candidates outside allowed template roots.
No run transcript demonstrates either a positive response or a hardened negative response.
observability.positive_marker: The intended final command is /readflag; the included challenge binary embeds a flag string.

preconditions: The described CTF provides WordPress 6.8.2 administrator credentials.
At least two posts are available or can be created.
The challenge deployment permits the relevant administrator option changes, has PEAR's pearcmd.php available, and has /readflag as the final command target.
The WordPress directory is read-only, which the writeup states blocks ordinary editor-based shell writes.

trigger_steps.summary: Request the PEAR post with config-create arguments, then request the shell post with parameter 0 set to the desired command.

impact.affected_asset: PHP process and filesystem of the challenge container, including the challenge /readflag executable's output.
impact.attacker_capability: A supplied WordPress administrator can cause creation and inclusion of /tmp/shell.php and request execution of an attacker-selected command through it in the challenge deployment.
impact.security_effect: Authenticated local file inclusion of selected PHP files, chained in the described container to PEAR config-create file writing and PHP command execution.

causal_trace.summary: The supplied administrator session can create posts, set percent-encoded post slugs, and set the stylesheet and upload_path options; the solver performs each of these actions.

Although literal slash and dot traversal characters are sanitized from a slug, get_single_template URL-decodes post_name before forming a single-post-{post_type}-{name}.php candidate. Thus encoded traversal becomes path syntax after the slug boundary; an administrator-controlled stylesheet root and the upload-created /tmp/single-post- prefix make the composed candidate resolve outside an approved theme directory.

locate_template checks file existence on the concatenation of the stylesheet path and candidate name, and the selected template is loaded. The writeup's constructed path uses the created prefix followed by decoded traversal to select an arbitrary existing .php target.

The documented chain first includes pearcmd.php with config-create arguments to write /tmp/shell.php, then selects that shell with the second controlled post and passes a command parameter; the bundled automation invokes /readflag. The bundled readflag binary contains a challenge flag string, but no execution transcript is supplied.

failure.operation: Existence check and subsequent load of a stylesheet-base/template-candidate concatenation that can resolve outside the theme root.

primary_invariant.statement: Every resolved template selected for inclusion must remain beneath an approved theme/template root after all decoding and path normalization.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The decoded slug supplies traversal segments after slug sanitization, while stylesheet controls the base used by template lookup and upload_path can create the required intermediate /tmp/single-post- directory.

raw_refs.role: author challenge writeup and mechanism excerpt

quality.review_notes: Mechanism is grounded in an author writeup that reproduces relevant WordPress function bodies and a complete automation script. The bundle lacks upstream WordPress source artifacts, deployment-script bodies proving PEAR availability and filesystem settings, an upstream patch or vendor acknowledgement, and a successful solver-run transcript. This record is limited to the deliberately configured WordPress 6.8.2 CTF deployment and does not establish general production applicability.

remediation.invariant_restored: After decoding and normalization, reject candidates or configured bases that do not resolve within approved template roots; do not permit option-controlled roots to escape those roots.
mitigation_classes: decode and canonicalize before path validation
enforce approved template-root containment after path resolution
restrict administrator control of template and upload root options

affected_versions_or_commits.value: WordPress 6.8.2 in the described challenge instance

target.component: single-post template resolution and administrator-controlled options

oracle.channel: HTTP requests issued by the supplied Playwright/curl solver
oracle.expected_negative: Encoded traversal slugs or stylesheet values that resolve outside approved template roots should not select or load the PEAR or shell target.
oracle.expected_positive: After administrator setup, the PEAR-target request is intended to create /tmp/shell.php and the shell-target request with command /readflag is intended to return that command's output.
